items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: So I met him downtown one day and I said, hey, Louis, big number.

ctx.x: So we had -- Costin, she was a ingenue and we had White Cliffs of Dover and we had the girls singing against it, you know, like a kind of melody, they'd sing the kind of melody and she'd sing the melody and they would fill in with words, so Louis Prima got somebody to sit in the audience to copy all the words and he told all of his band to copy all of their part.

So after he had left the theatre about six weeks or so like that, he put out this song, White Cliffs of Dover, Louis Prima and I said, to the guy hey that's my number. He took that from the theatre. So I met him downtown one day and I said, hey, Louis, big number. Yeah. I said, well you give me something for that.
